scope: Geometry, fill, stroke, user-space dashes and stroke adjustment checked against the local ISO 32000-2:2020 sponsored EC3 text. Exact-area antialiasing, flattening tolerance, half-open pixel boundaries and channel rounding are project policy. General zero-area scan conversion and minimum visible coverage remain unresolved.

requirements.status: signed cell-area and cover sweep; exact crossing-block integration
requirements.gaps: crossing-block/partial-row fallback remains superlinear in worst case; caller raster_work bounds it
requirements.rule: Nonzero and even-odd rules determine the filled region before scan conversion; exact-area antialiasing and 8-bit rounding are project policies.
Cubic Bézier geometry follows the specified control points; device-space approximation is subject to flatness tolerance.

requirements.status: user-space outlines, degenerate subpath classification and shared user-space dashing
requirements.gaps: Broader curve-stroke offset, curved-dash and extreme-coordinate independent vectors remain
requirements.rule: Width, caps, joins, miter limits and degenerate subpaths determine stroke geometry; cap and join styles are defined in Tables 53 and 54. Dashes restart per subpath and retain user-space distances.

requirements.status: orthogonal grid fitting with user-space dashes and rounded device pen diameters
requirements.rule: Automatic stroke adjustment fits thickness to device pixels, normally within half a pixel of the requested width, with sub-half-pixel widths rendered as single-pixel lines.

Dash array and phase measure user-space distance; negative phases are reduced by twice the array sum. Odd arrays reverse parity on each repetition. Each subpath restarts the pattern; empty arrays paint a solid line. Table 55 supplies exact run-sequence examples. Exact-area coverage and rounding are project policy.
requirements.status: user-space splitting before device hairline construction; Euclidean phase normalization
requirements.gaps: curve flattening is bounded by the device-space approximation policy

requirements.rule: A closed point or repeated coincident points stroke only with round caps; a trailing open move does not paint. A degenerate filled subpath encloses its device pixel and clipping uses that filled region. Half-open floor-cell ownership and antialias bytes are project policy.
requirements.status: point subpaths implemented for fills, clips and strokes
requirements.gaps: general collinear zero-area boundaries and minimum nonzero coverage need a scan-conversion policy decision
